changes: JSON CHANGE 1/3 — DFA a1 easy band renamed (v11.50 / v3.118): tiz_recovery → tiz_easy, and the short key recovery → easy in dfa_summary.tiz_pct, latest_session.tiz_split_pct and the dominant_band value. Band boundaries and values are unchanged. Hard rename, no dual emission — update any consumer keyed on dfa.tiz_recovery, tiz_pct.recovery, tiz_split_pct.recovery or dominant_band == "recovery".

JSON CHANGE 2/3 — intervals.json per-interval fields (v11.52 / v3.120): decoupling and avg_dfa_a1 are REMOVED. Neither is interpretable at segment scale — decoupling on a short or non-steady segment mainly reflects effort shape and HR lag, and each α1 value reflects a rolling window of preceding beats, so a short interval's average is dominated by carry-in. w_bal is replaced by w_bal_start / w_bal_end: the documented w_bal never existed upstream (the real fields are wbal_start / wbal_end) and therefore never produced a usable value. Activity-level decoupling and the session-level dfa block are unaffected.

JSON CHANGE 3/3 — DFA crossing eligibility (v11.54 / v3.122): a per-session crossing with reason "ok" is dwell-qualified but not necessarily usable. Consumers reading dfa.easy_guard_crossing / lt1_crossing / lt2_crossing in intervals.json must now ALSO require estimate_eligible. This one fails silently: avg_hr and avg_watts stay populated on a dwell-qualified but ineligible crossing as descriptive evidence, so old code reads a plausible number that Section 11 itself will not use as a threshold estimate. The latest.json rollups already gate on eligibility internally and need no change.

Sync no longer fails outright on present-but-null wellness fields (v11.56 / v3.124) — Intervals.icu returns sportInfo, sportSettings and sportSettings[].types with the key PRESENT and null, not absent, on records written by some third-party wellness clients. A .get(key, []) default applies only to an absent key, so the null reached the loop, raised TypeError and failed the entire sync. Athletes with no power meter were the most exposed, since sportInfo carries eFTP / W' / P-max and is most likely to be null precisely where it is least useful. Closes issue #23.

Interval data that used to go missing now arrives (v11.53 + v11.55 / v3.121 + v3.123) — two separate defects. Late upstream analysis was unrecoverable: an activity whose intervals were not yet analysed wrote no cache record at all, was re-fetched on every sync inside the 72-hour window, then became permanently unreachable once it aged out. Retries are now scheduled per endpoint with backoff, honouring Retry-After, and a transient streams failure no longer discards an already-successful interval fetch. Separately, intervals added or edited in Intervals.icu after a sync stayed invisible until intervals.json was deleted; the cache now invalidates on the activity's own sync token, at no extra API cost, and a failed refresh never costs the cached payload. Closes issue #20.

DFA a1 threshold estimates are stricter and will report less often (v11.54 / v3.122) — α1 is published from the prior 200 beats while power is instantaneous, so a crossing recorded across varying power blends work and recovery into a number that is not usable as a threshold estimate. Each crossing is now judged for power stationarity, artifact coverage and valid HR/power across its own span plus that beat lookback, and carries estimate_eligible / estimate_reason / n_eligible_segments. Expect some LT1/LT2 estimates that previously displayed to go null with a reason code — the old value was not trustworthy. Artifact reporting is corrected in the same pass: unknown artifact samples were padded with 0.0, which reported a perfect artifact rate for recordings carrying no artifact data at all and left the artifact filter silently inert. quality now carries artifact_state and artifact_coverage_pct.

Apple Watch HRV now explains itself (v11.58 / v3.126) — Apple's native HRV export is SDNN; the readiness signal is rMSSD, which Intervals.icu stores in a separate field. A wellness record carrying SDNN but no usable rMSSD produced signals.hrv.status "unavailable" with no stated cause. signals.hrv now carries an optional reason "rmssd_missing_sdnn_available" in exactly that case. No fallback and no conversion — SDNN and rMSSD are different time-domain measures and are not interchangeable. The repair is upstream of Intervals.icu: rMSSD has to be derived from beat-to-beat data before the wellness record is written. Readiness behaviour is unchanged. Closes issue #25.

Also in this batch: per-interval min_hr, with four HR-recovery coaching criteria suspended because no emitted field ever defined them (v11.51 / v3.119, issue #19); VirtualRow joins the rowing sport family instead of falling through to other (v11.57 / v3.125, issue #22); new activity-level zone_basis stating whether a segment zone number means power, HR or pace, omitted when it cannot be established (v11.52); new intervals.json schema_version, currently 1, independent of the producer version (v11.52); dominant_band now selected on raw band secs with exact ties resolved by descending intensity rather than alphabetically (v11.50).
Upgrade: after replacing the affected files — at minimum sync.py — run sync twice manually, or wait for two scheduled runs to complete.
